subject: [P1] ProspectShield: sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts after SDK update
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@prospectshield.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: ProspectShield Engineering <eng@prospectshield.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts after SDK update

Hi Naomi / Marissa —

We're seeing a production outage that started ~13:50 UTC. Our services are getting a mix of 429s and 5xx from Redwood endpoints and client timeouts. Traffic shape is normal for us (no sudden surge on our side), but latency has climbed and our downstream workers are retrying aggressively which amplifies the problem.

Quick summary:
- Error types: 429 (rate limited), 503 and intermittent 504 timeouts.
- First observed: 2026-08-29T13:50:21Z
- Impact: requests failing for ~25% of requests to the inference route used by our personalization pipeline.
- Recent change: we rolled the latest Redwood JS SDK 2.4.0 at 13:30 UTC.

I've attached a sample log with request IDs and a screenshot of the client timeline. We're blocked on our real-time personalization flow — can you triage urgently? Please escalate to engineering; Mary (CFO) is CC'd as this is affecting revenue-critical flows.

Attachments:
- prospectshield_429_sample.log (text/log)
- screenshot-429-sequence.png

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm whether this is a Redwood-side capacity/regression.
2) If it's client-driven retry amplification, advise quick mitigations (rate-limiting, turning down retries on our SDK) we can push immediately.
3) Provide ETA for a mitigation or rollback.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform — ProspectShield
alex@prospectshield.com

Folks — forwarding urgent report from ProspectShield (DEAL-8923). They upgraded to our SDK v2.4.0 ~40 minutes ago and are seeing elevated 429/5xx and timeouts. External customer reports retries are amplifying the issue.

Immediate asks for SRE/Runtime team:
- Marcus: can you triage and verify whether the spikes originate in our serving layer or if client retry patterns are causing cascading failures?
- Connor: can you pull edge routing metrics and recent scaling activity for the us-east region?
- Marissa: loop CS for customer comms; I will send an interim note to Alex.

Please post a short triage note here with observed root cause indicators and recommended short-term mitigations (minutes) + longer-term fixes (hours). This needs exec visibility if it's a platform regression.

Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts after SDK update

Quick triage notes — initial findings: 

1) Observed symptom: sudden increase in 429 responses at the gateway and a corresponding increase in pending requests on several inference pools. Gateway logs show repeated retries from the same client IP ranges.

2) Correlation with SDK: we see a spike in client-user-agent header to "RedwoodJS/2.4.0" starting 13:32 UTC. Prior to that, request rate was stable.

3) Root cause hypothesis: retry amplification. The SDK default retry/backoff in v2.4.0 sets RTT-based fast retries without sufficient jitter or backoff clamping. Under transient latency, clients issue immediate re-attempts which the gateway treats as new requests, saturating worker queues and returning 429/503.

4) Evidence: sample request IDs from prospectshield_429_sample.log show 4–6 identical request IDs (same trace key) issued within 2s windows. Gateway queue depth spikes linearly after these bursts.

Short-term mitigations (minutes):
- Apply a rate limit rule scoped to ProspectShield API key at the edge (throttle to their baseline RPS).
- Inject a 50ms server-side retry-suppress header (X-Redwood-Retry-Suppress: true) for requests that match duplicate trace keys so backend doesn't double-process duplicates — locking change already approved in our routing tier and can be enabled as a config flip.
- Recommend ProspectShield immediately downgrade SDK or set retries to 1 with exponential backoff + jitter. We should send exact config snippet.

Mid-term (hours):
- Patch SDK defaults to include jitter and max backoff clamp (v2.4.1) and push advisory.
- Add detection rule for client-side retry storms and automatic soft-throttle fallback to protect shared pools.

I'll stage the edge rate-limit and the routing config now. Connor, please confirm if pool autoscaling prevented worker OOMs — initial metrics show scaling at ~13:55 but it lagged.

Attachment: excerpt of gateway log lines: 
"[2026-08-29T13:52:06Z] req=aa3f... client=52.21.9.32 path=/v1/generate status=429 queue=24
[2026-08-29T13:52:06Z] req=aa3f... client=52.21.9.32 path=/v1/generate status=429 queue=30
[2026-08-29T13:52:07Z] req=aa3f... client=52.21.9.32 path=/v1/generate status=503 backend=timeout"

Marcus
Staff Engineer, Runtime

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@prospectshield.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, ProspectShield Engineering <eng@prospectshield.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike and timeouts after SDK update

Alex — thank you for the quick report and logs. We have an initial plan: 

What we've done (live):
- Enabled an edge-scoped rate limit for ProspectShield's API key to their baseline RPS to stop amplification.
- Flipped routing config to set X-Redwood-Retry-Suppress for suspected duplicate requests.

Why this happened: our runtime telemetry shows a large number of immediate client retries originating from instances using RedwoodJS/2.4.0. The SDK defaults changed retry behavior in a way that can exacerbate transient latency into a retry storm. Marcus is preparing an advisory & SDK patch.

Immediate ask for ProspectShield (small change you can push now):
- In your SDK config set: retries: 1, backoff: { type: "exponential", base_ms: 200, max_ms: 2000, jitter: true }

Next steps:
- Marcus will publish a short tech note and we will issue a customer advisory with SDK v2.4.1 that tightens defaults.
- Marissa will coordinate an incident summary and an ETA for follow-up remediation.
- Naomi will schedule a 30-min technical call at 16:00 UTC to walk through logs and next steps.

We understand the severity — we will follow up with an incident timeline and any credit considerations.
